checks: On the compact product, the mean-value bound for φ on the convex hull of tuple averages gives the separate cost bounds λ_i sup|∇φ|. Every maximizing coupling uses equality for the same chosen dual tuple.

The fixed-other-coordinate maximum defining U_i is finite and continuous by compactness; subtracting (ελ_i²/2)|v|² leaves a maximum of convex functions. On K_i the maximum is at most u_i. At an equality tuple the other coordinates realize the maximum, so the touching smooth term supports U_i with subgradient +λ_i∇φ(b(x)). The extensions are separate and do not need to be jointly feasible off the compact product. For k=1, U_1=φ.

Finite strong convexity gives a quadratic lower bound from a subgradient at the origin; subtracting p·v preserves coercivity and strong convexity. Strong monotonicity yields |T(p)−T(q)|≤|p−q|/κ, and the two optimizing-point bounds have error at most |h|²/κ around h·T(p). Thus V_i=U_i* is finite, convex, C¹ with global gradient bound 1/(ελ_i²).

The subgradient condition identifies x_i uniquely as T_i(λ_i∇φ(b(x))). The composition is locally Lipschitz because ∇φ is C¹. Pushing forward an optimizer by b transfers the endpoint identities to the exact marginal laws, and substituting the endpoint identities back into b gives the weighted sum identity almost everywhere.

dependencies.mapping: K_i=supp γ_i are nonempty compact, their masses agree and are positive, and φ∘b is separately Lipschitz by the compact mean-value estimate. The predecessor supplies an optimal dual tuple and equality under every optimizer.

overlap.comparison: The McCann input in this proof has a forward endpoint-to-endpoint gradient map for two absolutely continuous marginals. It does not recover each endpoint from the barycenter for a common family of maximizers of arbitrary strongly convex surplus, including singular marginals.

readability: The uniform claim over every maximizing coupling follows from the nonnegative duality gap for the same dual tuple.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: A single optimal compact dual tuple yields global strongly convex extensions and Lipschitz conjugate gradients that recover the endpoints for every maximizing coupling, with no absolute continuity premise.
